title: Explicit insert into GENERATED ALWAYS identity fails
expected_feedback: Standard: for an identity column defined as GENERATED ALWAYS it is an error to insert an explicit value without OVERRIDING SYSTEM VALUE, so this copy fails at runtime with 'cannot insert a non-DEFAULT value into column id'. Either declare the column GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY, or write INSERT INTO orders_new (id, ...) OVERRIDING SYSTEM VALUE SELECT .... Remember to advance the identity sequence with setval before the swap, guarding the empty-table case with coalesce. Also: the bulk INSERT ... SELECT loads orders_new with no ANALYZE afterwards, so the new table takes traffic with no planner statistics at all -- worse than stale ones. Run ANALYZE orders_new before the swap.
violated_rule: explicit identity insert requires OVERRIDING SYSTEM VALUE
